title: secp256k1-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on order-6 classes with a sigma walk, all arithmetic in instructions

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the order-6 classes given by negation and the GLV endomorphism, using 2^32 walks, 2^16 adders, batched affine additions and deterministic fruitless-cycle escapes. Walks run in trails from fresh coins: each trail ends at its first distinguished point, which it records once with its coins, and the first key match is resolved by replaying the two trails, so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D) and the replay is bounded and charged. The walk stores actual points and adds the tabulated image sigma(R_i) of each adder, so the class sequence equals the standard canonical walk while no step multiplies by beta; the canonical rotation is decided from 64-bit fixed-point fractions with an exact fallback (Lemma 1). Total computation is at most 2^126.418986 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, all failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output. No reference operation is claimed: each walk step, a batched incomplete affine addition in the package's own 4x64-bit inline-assembly field arithmetic, is charged at most 795 scalar AArch64 instructions at C=1000 (0.795 units), against 780.0 measured with the organizer's Callgrind toolchain on two input sets; the Python replica matches every final point. Peak memory is at most 2^75.74996 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^47.61967 units and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound of 0.411523 relies on the disclosed heuristics H1-H3 in proof.md. H1 is the standard random-mapping model for r-adding class walks with an exponent penalty of at most 4/2^16; H2 bounds fruitless-cycle rates; H3 is the representativeness of the measured instruction counts. These are supported by toy-curve runs of the identical procedure and by production-curve measurements, not proved. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a claim of a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the complete procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on random prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3+7 (b=7, the secp256k1 shape) or y^2=x^3+4 subgroups (b=4), at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4: each slot runs trails from fresh coins without tracking coefficients, with the same class key, canonical rule, adder images and index, both cycle rules and escapes; a trail ends at its first distinguished point, recorded once with its coins, or is abandoned at the cap; each slot takes L steps and finishes its trail. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails from their coins (with a different anchor schedule, checking Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only: it tests the procedure and its collision statistics, not production cost.

Check Lemma 1 of proof.md on random and edge-case reduced values: the 64-bit fraction approximations g_0 = a_3 and g_1 (4x64-bit limbs) are within [0,1] and [0,8] of floor(2^64*(beta^j x mod p)/p), and the kernel's rule for the canonical rotation either agrees with the exact minimum or falls back to the exact computation.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters with exact integer arithmetic.
